title:
FRACTIONS, DECIMALS AND PERCENTAGES
(RECURRING DECIMALS)
objective: LO: I can convert recurring decimals to fractions using algebraic methods.

content.text: Recurring decimals have one or more digits that REPEAT forever. We write a dot above the repeating digit(s): 0.3̇ means 0.333... and 0.1̇2̇ means 0.121212...
Key fact: Every recurring decimal can be written as an exact fraction. Terminating decimals have denominators whose only prime factors are 2 and 5.

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Let x = the recurring decimal. Multiply by 10 (or 100, 1000...) to shift the repeating block. Subtract to eliminate the recurring part. Solve for x.
key_idea.caption: Multiply, subtract, simplify

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – one repeating digit
modelled_examples.question: Convert 0.4̇ to a fraction
modelled_examples.explanation: One repeating digit: multiply by 10. Subtract x from 10x to get 9x = 4.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – two repeating digits
modelled_examples.question: Convert 0.6̇3̇ to a fraction
modelled_examples.explanation: Two repeating digits: multiply by 100. Subtract: 99x = 63. Simplify: 63/99 = 7/11.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – non-repeating start
modelled_examples.question: Convert 0.16̇ to a fraction
modelled_examples.explanation: The 1 doesn’t repeat, but the 6 does. Use 100x − 10x = 90x to eliminate the recurring part.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – three repeating digits
modelled_examples.question: Convert 0.1̇23̇ to a fraction
modelled_examples.explanation: Three repeating digits: multiply by 1000. Subtract: 999x = 123. Simplify: 123/999 = 41/333.

practice.heading: Identify the recurring part
practice.instruction: Write the first 6 decimal places and underline the repeating block.

practice.heading: One repeating digit → fraction
practice.instruction: Convert each recurring decimal to a fraction. Simplify where possible.

practice.heading: Two repeating digits → fraction
practice.instruction: Convert each recurring decimal to a fraction. Use ×100 and subtract.

practice.heading: Non-repeating start → fraction
practice.instruction: Convert each recurring decimal to a fraction. Careful: part of the decimal doesn’t repeat.

items.statement: 0.1̇2̇ means multiply by 100 to shift the block
0.16̇ needs 100x − 10x to eliminate the recurring part

problems.text:
Prove algebraically that 0.9̇ = 1.
Let x = 0.999... and use the multiply-and-subtract method. Explain why this proves they are equal.

A student says “&frac17; = 0.142857̇” (with a dot only over the 7).
Explain why this is wrong. What is the correct dot notation for &frac17;? How many digits repeat?
